record.paper_title: Two Open Problems in the Fixed Point Theory of Contractive Type Mappings on First-Countable Quasimetric Spaces
record.context_brief: Fixed points of contractions on complete F-symmetric spaces
record.original_question: Let (X, d) be a complete F-symmetric space. This means that d is a distance satisfying d(x, y) >= 0 for all x, y in X and d(x, y) + d(y, x) = 0 if and only if x = y, that d is symmetric in the sense that d(x, y) = d(y, x) for all x, y in X, and that d satisfies the F-condition: for every epsilon > 0 there exists delta = delta(epsilon) > 0 such that d(x, y) <= delta and d(y, z) <= delta imply d(x, z) <= epsilon. A sequence {x_n} is Cauchy if lim_{n,m->infinity} d(x_n, x_m) = 0, converges to x if lim_{n->infinity} d(x, x_n) = 0, and the space is complete if every Cauchy sequence converges in this sense. If g : X -> X is a contraction, meaning that there exists a constant lambda with 0 <= lambda < 1 such that d(g(x), g(y)) <= lambda d(x, y) for all x, y in X, must g have a fixed point?

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Let g : X −→ X be a contraction of a complete F-symmetric space (X, d). Is it true that g has fixed points?
We say that a distance space (X, d) is complete if every Cauchy sequence in X converges to some point in X.
If d is a distance on X such that: (iiim) d(x, y) = d(y, x), for all x, y ∈ X, then (X, d) is called a symmetric space and d is called a symmetric on X.

(F) for any ε > 0 there exists δ = δ(ε) > 0 such that from d(x, y) ≤ δ and d(y, z) ≤ δ it follows d(x, z) ≤ ε, then d is called an F-distance or a Fréchet distance and (X, d) is called an F-distance space.

A mapping ϕ : X → X is called: (i) Lipschitzian or λ-Lipschitzian if there exists λ > 0 such that d(ϕ(x), ϕ(y)) ≤ λ · d(x, y), for all x, y ∈ X; (ii) contraction or λ-contraction if it is λ-Lipschitzian with 0 ≤ λ < 1;

We give a complete answer to the first problem, a partial answer to the second one, and also illustrate the complexity and relevance of these problems by means of four very interesting and comprehensive examples.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a nonempty set. A function $d:X\times X\to\mathbb{R}$ is called a distance on $X$ if for all $x,y\in X$:
(i) $d(x,y)\ge 0$, and
(ii) $d(x,y)+d(y,x)=0$ if and only if $x=y$.

Assume in addition that $d$ is symmetric, i.e. $d(x,y)=d(y,x)$ for all $x,y\in X$, and that $d$ satisfies the F-condition (Fréchet condition):
for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta=\delta(\varepsilon)>0$ such that whenever $x,y,z\in X$ satisfy $d(x,y)\le\delta$ and $d(y,z)\le\delta$, one has $d(x,z)\le\varepsilon$.

A space $(X,d)$ satisfying all of the above is called an F-symmetric space.

Define convergence and Cauchy sequences as follows. A sequence $\{x_n\}\subset X$ converges to $x\in X$ if $\lim_{n\to\infty}d(x,x_n)=0$. A sequence $\{x_n\}$ is Cauchy if $\lim_{n,m\to\infty}d(x_n,x_m)=0$. The space $(X,d)$ is complete if every Cauchy sequence in $X$ converges to some point of $X$.

A map $g:X\to X$ is called a contraction if there exists $\lambda\in[0,1)$ such that
$$d(g(x),g(y))\le \lambda\, d(x,y)\quad\text{for all } x,y\in X.$$

Question: Must every contraction $g$ on a complete F-symmetric space $(X,d)$ have a fixed point?

artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a published resolution of this specific question about contractions on complete F-symmetric (Fréchet symmetric) spaces. Related work exists for f-quasimetric spaces and F-contractions in metric spaces, but no source confirms whether the existence of a fixed point for arbitrary Banach-type contractions on complete F-symmetric spaces has been proved or disproved. The status is therefore not verifiable from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: The Fixed Points of Contractions of f-Quasimetric Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Extends the Banach Contraction Mapping Principle and related theorems on generalized contractions to mappings of f-quasimetric spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related but distinct setting (f-quasimetric, not F-symmetric); does not directly settle the F-symmetric problem.

status_evidence.title: Fixed point theorems for F-contractions (Wardowski-type)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops fixed point theory for F-contractions in metric spaces endowed with a graph.
status_evidence.claim: Different notion of 'F-contraction'; not addressing F-symmetric spaces.
